question: In adults having primary elective hip or knee replacement without renal impairment, what proportion receive both intravenous and topical tranexamic acid, with a total dose of 3 g or less?
why: NICE asks for IV plus topical TXA, but most units give IV only. The one arthroplasty audit in the corpus found combined use in 7% [1680]; hip replacement has not been audited.

standard.wording: For primary elective hip or knee replacement: Give intravenous tranexamic acid. If there is no renal impairment, also apply 1 g to 2 g of topical (intra-articular) tranexamic acid diluted in saline after the final wash-out and before wound closure. Ensure that the total combined dose of tranexamic acid does not exceed 3 g.

pass: No renal impairment: IV TXA given and 1–2 g topical TXA recorded, total 3 g or less. Mild or moderate renal impairment: reduced-dose IV TXA only.
population: Include adults having primary elective THR, TKR or UKR. Exclude revisions, fractures and severe renal impairment (TXA contraindicated).
sample: 40 consecutive primary hip and knee replacements over the last 2–3 months
data_source: Anaesthetic chart and theatre drug record (IV dose); operation note or scrub record (topical dose); pre-assessment eGFR from EPR.

question: In adults having primary elective shoulder replacement, what proportion receive intravenous tranexamic acid or have a recorded reason for not giving it?

standard.wording: For primary elective shoulder replacement: Consider intravenous tranexamic acid. If there is no renal impairment, consider 1 g to 2 g of topical (intra-articular) tranexamic acid diluted in saline applied after the final wash-out and before wound closure. Ensure that the total combined dose of tranexamic acid does not exceed 3 g.

pass: IV TXA given at or before incision, or a reason for not giving it written on the anaesthetic chart or op note.
population: Include adults having primary elective anatomic, reverse or hemi shoulder replacement. Exclude fractures and revisions.
sample: All primary elective shoulder replacements over the last 6–12 months (usually 30–50 in a DGH)
data_source: Theatre system list (OPCS W49–W51, W96–W98); anaesthetic chart; operation note; EPR eGFR.

question: In adults found to have iron-deficiency anaemia at pre-assessment for primary hip or knee replacement, what proportion were offered iron before surgery?
why: Preoperative anaemia predicts transfusion [1472]. Orthopaedic anaemia audits are few (3 in corpus) and mostly old.

standard.source: NICE NG24 recs 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 (2015); NICE NG180 rec 1.3.4 (2020)
standard.wording: Offer oral iron before and after surgery to people with iron‑deficiency anaemia. [2015] Consider intravenous iron before or after surgery for people who: have iron‑deficiency anaemia and cannot tolerate or absorb oral iron, or are unable to adhere to oral iron treatment are diagnosed with functional iron deficiency are diagnosed with iron‑deficiency anaemia, and the interval between the diagnosis of anaemia and surgery is predicted to be too short for oral iron to be effective. [2015]

pass: Oral or IV iron prescribed or recommended to the GP before the surgery date.
population: Include adults with Hb below the local anaemia cut-off and ferritin low (or iron studies showing deficiency) at arthroplasty pre-assessment. Exclude anaemia of other cause.
sample: 30–40 consecutive anaemic pre-assessment patients over the last 6 months
data_source: Pre-assessment records; pathology (Hb, ferritin, TSAT); EPR or GP letter for iron; day unit list for IV iron.

why: Routine dipsticks lead to needless antibiotics and delays. One corpus arthroplasty QI stopped routine MSUs as part of a bundle [1591], but none measured it.

standard.wording: Do not routinely offer urine dipstick tests before surgery. Consider microscopy and culture of midstream urine sample before surgery if the presence of a urinary tract infection would influence the decision to operate.

question: In adults listed for primary hip or knee replacement, what proportion have prehabilitation advice on exercise, weight and smoking recorded before surgery?
why: NICE asks for prehab advice for everyone, but it is rarely recorded. Corpus smoking and weight audits are in trauma [1336] or measured weight loss [1273], not advice at listing.

standard.wording: Give people having hip or knee replacement advice on preoperative rehabilitation. Include advice on: exercises to do before and after surgery that will aid recovery lifestyle, including weight management, diet and smoking cessation (see NICE's guidance on lifestyle and wellbeing) maximising functional independence and quality of life before and after surgery.

pass: Clinic letter, pre-assessment or joint school record shows advice on exercises and lifestyle (weight and, if a smoker, smoking) before surgery.
population: Include adults having primary elective THR, TKR or UKR.
sample: 40 consecutive patients over the last 2 months
data_source: Listing letter, pre-assessment form, joint school register.
